Subject: Redwood Private VPC vs Hyperscaler — next steps + network questions

Hi Elena — great meeting today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood: 

- Summary: You shared that AcmeHealth wants predictable inference latency for PHI workloads, full control of network egress, and the ability to run in an air-gapped environment for certain clinics. Your primary competitors in evaluation are the major hyperscalers and CloudCorp.
- Redwood differentiation we highlighted: private control plane option (VPC peering + customer-managed KMS), optional on-prem air-gapped package, and lightweight control plane that can be deployed in your VPC for auditability.

Proposed next tests (we should align on order):
1) Networking validation: provide a minimal set of IPs/ports and test connectivity from your subnet to the Redwood control plane endpoint; validate egress policies.
2) Control plane review: we’ll share a one-pager and an architecture diagram for how the control plane behaves in private mode (no outbound telemetry by default).
3) Air-gap feasibility: a checklist + runbook for an on-prem package and a short POC to validate model artifact transfer and offline inference.

Action items for AcmeHealth:
- Please share the security questionnaire you typically use for vendor evaluations (we can pre-fill).
- Confirm whether you prefer we start with networking validation or the control plane review first.

Attachments: redwood-private-vs-hyperscaler-onepager.pdf, redwood-vpc-airgap-arch-diagram.png

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up for the week of Oct 5 unless you want to propose another cadence.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi Elena — looping in answers to the specific technical Qs below. Happy to jump on a short call with your infra lead to walk through when you’re ready.

Networking (minimal):
- Outbound: control-plane.redwood-inference.com (TCP 443). For POC we can provide an FQDN and a static IP range to allow in your egress ACLs.
- Model transfer: SFTP over port 22 for the air-gapped transfer workflow, or signed OCI bundles via your internal registry if you prefer.

Telemetry & control plane:
- In private mode the control plane runs in your VPC and by default does NOT send telemetry off-network. We provide an opt-in telemetry agent if you want usage/latency metrics captured in Redwood Console. License checks are token-based and can be configured to validate against your internal auth (no external call required if you run the private control plane).

Air-gapped POC checklist (high-level):
- Two worker hosts (NVIDIA T4 or equivalent) for inference testing (we’ll provide a minimum CPU/RAM spec for the control plane).
- A bastion host for model ingestion (SFTP) or an offline USB transfer procedure; signed model bundles from Redwood.
- Timeline: 1 week for infra prep, 1 week to transfer & validate model artifacts, 1 week for inference validation and perf comparison vs your baseline.

Attachments: I’ll attach the architecture diagram and a short checklist as separate files in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — quick note on pricing/engagement options so you can plan internally.

Options:
1) Hosted private control plane (VPC-based): monthly usage + control plane subscription. Fastest to stand up (days) and supports customer-managed KMS.
2) Dedicated reserved capacity: committed monthly/annual GPU pool, predictable throughput, SLA-backed. Good if you need sustained inference at scale.
3) On-prem air-gapped install: one-time deployment + annual support license. Includes transfer tooling and an agreed maintenance window cadence.

For the POC you asked about, we can do a short on-prem pilot scoped as a fixed-fee engagement (covers deployment, model transfer, and 2-week validation). I’ve included a sample SOW outline in the one-pager we shared earlier.

If you want, Vanessa and I can produce a combined costs/options sheet tailored to your expected qps and model sizes. Would that help your procurement team?
